options.content:
# 🔵 Base Devnet Control Room
Live operational view from **RPC ingress → HA sequencing → execution → derivation → L1 batch publication**. Use the node filters to isolate a role or instance; deep links for profiles, raw metrics, and traces are above.

panels.description: Share of all expected Base node, conductor, and batcher scrape targets currently reachable. A missing target remains visible as down rather than being converted to zero data.
panels.title: Telemetry Reachability

panels.description: The unified sequencer currently advertising active=true. Only the current leader is returned; a blank panel means no sequencer reports active.
panels.title: Active Sequencer

panels.description: Latest unsafe L2 block accepted by the active builder consensus node.
panels.title: L2 Unsafe Head

panels.description: Completed builder timing observations per minute. This is the reliable liveness signal for build cycles; it does not claim every cycle contained user transactions.
panels.title: Build Throughput

panels.description: Successful share of active JSON-RPC calls across Base Reth nodes. No traffic remains N/A rather than being shown as 100% successful.
panels.title: RPC Success

panels.description: Minimum startup state across the three op-conductor members. This verifies process readiness; detailed health-check and commit behavior appear in the HA row.
panels.title: Conductor Readiness
Chain Progress · Are all nodes advancing together?

panels.description: Unsafe L2 head reported by every selected execution/consensus node. Parallel lines indicate agreement; separation identifies a lagging or isolated node.
panels.title: Unsafe Head Agreement

panels.description: Active builder's unsafe, safe, and finalized labels. These are absolute block heights; the gap panel below makes divergence easier to compare.
panels.title: Builder Safety & Finality

panels.description: Block gaps between the builder's unsafe→safe and safe→finalized labels. Devnet finality depends on accelerated block cadence and L1 timing, so trends matter more than universal thresholds.
panels.title: Safety & Finality Gaps

panels.description: Worst timestamp age for unsafe, safe, and finalized block references across the selected fleet. Unlike scrape age, this measures chain data freshness; the logarithmic axis preserves visibility across sub-second and multi-minute ages.
panels.title: Worst Block Reference Age
HA & Conductor · Is leadership healthy and commits flowing?

panels.description: Current role of all three HA sequencer members. Active, standby, and abnormal recovery states are visually distinct.

targets.expr: max by(instance) (reth_base_node_sequencer_state{job=~"l2_builder|l2_sequencer",active="false",recovery="false"}) or 2 * max by(instance) (reth_base_node_sequencer_state{job=~"l2_builder|l2_sequencer",active="true",recovery="false"}) or 3 * max by(instance) (reth_base_node_sequencer_state{job=~"l2_builder|l2_sequencer",recovery="true"})

panels.title: Sequencer Role State

panels.description: Unsafe payload commit requests handled by each conductor. In steady state the active leader owns this traffic; a line handoff makes failover visible.
panels.title: Unsafe Payload Commits

panels.description: Cluster-wide commitUnsafePayload latency calculated from the conductor histogram. These are mergeable quantiles, unlike client-side summary quantiles.
panels.title: Commit Latency

panels.description: Health-check failures per conductor, derived as total checks minus successful checks so a healthy zero remains visible instead of becoming No data.
panels.title: Conductor Health-Check Failures

panels.description: p99 conductor control-loop iteration duration per member. The loop normally tracks the configured health-check cadence; sustained growth indicates control-plane saturation.
panels.title: Conductor Loop p99
Base Consensus · Can the rollup pipeline keep up?

panels.description: Worst exported p99 Engine API request latency among selected nodes, split by method. Summary quantiles are not averaged across instances.
panels.title: Engine API · Worst Node p99

panels.description: Engine API request throughput by method across selected nodes. forkchoiceUpdated naturally occurs more often than full payload builds.
panels.title: Engine API Throughput

panels.description: Pending consensus engine tasks per selected node. Healthy steady state is typically zero; persistent depth indicates the engine cannot keep pace.
panels.title: Engine Task Queue Depth

panels.description: L1 origin consumed by each selected derivation pipeline. A flat or separated line identifies a node whose rollup derivation has stalled or fallen behind.
panels.title: Derivation L1 Origin

panels.description: Latest L2 block stepped by each derivation pipeline. This is pipeline output progress, not a replacement for the safe head label.
panels.title: Derived L2 Block

panels.description: Worst selected-node depth at three derivation stages. Sustained growth localizes backpressure to frames, channels, or payload attributes.
panels.title: Derivation Buffer Depth
Block Builder · Are payloads fast and useful?

panels.description: Builder end-to-end duration summary at p50, p90, and p99. Quantiles come from one builder instance and are safe to display directly.
panels.title: End-to-End Build Latency

panels.description: Completed end-to-end build timing observations per second. Each observation is one completed build cycle, making this a reliable builder liveness and throughput signal.
panels.title: Build Cycles

panels.description: Mean and exported p99 transaction count per payload. Mean is computed from summary sum/count; p99 comes directly from the single builder summary.
panels.title: Transactions per Payload

panels.description: p99 latency comparison for end-to-end building, state-root calculation, and builder-side getPayload. This puts the largest critical-path contributor in context without mixing units.
panels.title: Builder Critical Path · p99
Batch Publication · Is L2 data reaching L1 efficiently?

panels.description: Blocks waiting in either batcher implementation, op-batcher channels held in memory, and base-batcher frames ready for submission. Channels and frames are implementation-specific and are shown separately. A sawtooth is normal as channels close and submit; sustained growth without submissions indicates backpressure.
panels.title: Batcher Backlog

panels.description: L1 submission outcomes per second, shown separately for op-batcher stages and base-batcher outcomes. Submitted and successful or confirmed transactions should track; failed or requeued outcomes identify publication instability.
panels.title: L1 Submission Outcomes

panels.description: Raw channel input and compressed output bytes per second from either batcher implementation, plus base-batcher L1 DA bytes submitted. The relative lines make compression and publication flow visible.
panels.title: Batch Data Throughput

panels.description: Mean transaction-manager send latency calculated from mergeable summary sum/count values. The exported unit is milliseconds.
panels.title: L1 Transaction Send Latency

panels.description: Channel compression ratio from op-batcher histograms or base-batcher summary quantiles. Lower output/input ratios mean stronger compression; the fallback keeps the incompatible metric representations separate.
panels.title: Channel Compression Ratio

panels.description: Current L1 balance of the batch submitter account, reported in ether.
panels.title: Batcher Balance

panels.description: Implementation-specific batcher status. For op-batcher, STARTING/READY reports startup completion. For base-batcher, DISABLED/MISMATCH/ALIGNED reports shadow parity validation; it does not report service readiness.
panels.title: Batcher Status
RPC · Is the devnet responsive to users and services?

panels.description: JSON-RPC request rate by selected node role. This includes internal devnet traffic and makes unexpected concentration visible.
panels.title: RPC Request Rate

panels.description: Failed / started JSON-RPC calls by selected node role. Idle roles remain N/A instead of being forced to zero success or zero error.
panels.title: RPC Error Ratio

panels.description: Eight busiest active JSON-RPC method/role pairs in the current rate window. The >0 filter excludes hundreds of registered but idle methods.
panels.title: Top Active RPC Methods

panels.description: Mean server time for the eight slowest currently active method/role pairs. Positive-count filtering removes idle NaN series before top-k selection.

targets.expr: topk(8, (sum by(job,method) (rate(reth_rpc_server_calls_time_seconds_sum{job=~"$node_job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by(job,method) (rate(reth_rpc_server_calls_time_seconds_count{job=~"$node_job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))) and on(job,method) (sum by(job,method) (rate(reth_rpc_server_calls_time_seconds_count{job=~"$node_job",instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) > 0))

panels.title: Slowest Active RPC Methods · Mean
Fleet, P2P & Runtime · Is a node or resource becoming the bottleneck?

panels.description: Execution-network and Base consensus gossip peer counts by selected role. Both should remain stable; divergence can distinguish execution P2P from consensus gossip issues.
panels.title: Minimum Peer Count

panels.description: Fleet-wide execution P2P activity for active sessions and transaction propagation. Compare message and transaction flow to spot stalled or unexpectedly quiet networking.
panels.title: P2P Message Rate

panels.description: Fleet-wide active-session backpressure and transaction-send errors. Both should remain at zero; stacked bars are valid because these are additive error events.
panels.title: P2P Backpressure & Errors

panels.description: Process CPU seconds consumed per second by selected Base Reth nodes. Values are CPU cores, not host percentages, because cgroup limits are not scraped.
panels.title: Node CPU

panels.description: Resident memory by selected Base Reth node. This is process RSS; container limits and host pressure require a cgroup exporter not currently present in devnet.
panels.title: Node Resident Memory

panels.description: Worst Prometheus scrape duration per Base service role. This is both a telemetry freshness check and an early warning for oversized or slow metric endpoints.
panels.title: Metrics Scrape Duration

panels.description: Total user + system CPU consumed inside newPayload processing by selected node role, expressed as CPU-seconds per second (cores). Use Profiles for function-level attribution.
panels.title: newPayload CPU Cost

panels.description: Fleet-wide major and minor page faults during newPayload processing. Major faults imply disk-backed paging and should remain at zero; minor faults expose memory-mapping churn.
panels.title: newPayload Page Faults
